mainTopic: The ברכות over natural wonders in the משנה: earthquakes, thunder, winds, lightning, the rainbow, mountains and a clear sky
overview: This amud goes through the משנה's list of natural wonders that get a ברכה. It opens by finishing an אגדה about the stars כימה and עיש and the מבול, and רב נחמן says עיש will get its stars back in the future. For זוועות, רב קטינא says they are earthquakes. He publicly calls a necromancer who explained them as הקדוש ברוך הוא's tears a liar, though the גמרא says he did so only so people would not follow the necromancer, and several חכמים give their own explanations. For thunder, many explanations are offered, and the גמרא favors רב אחא בר יעקב's link to lightning. אביי explains the משנה's 'winds' as gale-force winds, and רבא lists lightning and cloud patterns that are warning signs at night. The amud teaches the ברכה over a rainbow: we do not bow, but we say 'זוכר הברית ונאמן בבריתו וקיים במאמרו'. אביי and רבא explain how 'עושה מעשה בראשית' relates to lightning and to mountains. Finally, רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a ברכה for a perfectly clear sky, and רב חסדא says such a sky has not been seen since the חורבן.

steps.title: Why עיש follows כימה: the stars of the flood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes describing the stars. It explains that עיש follows כימה to demand back two stars that were taken from it to close the gap left by the מבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: …like something that was torn off and attached. And the reason עיש goes after כימה is that it is saying to it: 'Give me my children!' When הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to bring a flood on the world, He took two stars from כימה and brought the flood. When He wanted to close it up, He took two stars from עיש and closed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The first two words finish a description that began earlier in the daf. Then the גמרא tells a story explaining why one constellation (עיש) seems to chase another (כימה) across the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing two stars from כימה opened the way for the waters of the מבול. To seal that opening, הקדוש ברוך הוא used two stars taken from עיש. So עיש is 'missing' two stars, and the picture is that it follows כימה demanding them back.

keyTerms.meaning: A star cluster, usually identified with the Pleiades
A constellation, usually identified with Ursa Major (or Aldebaran)
The flood in the days of נח
Give me my children (here, the two missing stars)
To close it up / seal the opening

steps.confusionAlert: The two words כטרפא דטריף belong to the description at the end of the previous section. Do not read them as part of the 'give me my children' story.

phrases.english: like a leaf/piece that was attached (torn off and attached).
phrases.notes: Tail end of the previous description of the stars.

phrases.english: And the fact that it (עיש) goes after it (כימה),
is because it says to it: Give me my children.
For at the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
sought to bring a flood into the world,
He took two stars from Kimah (Pleiades)
and brought a flood upon the world.
And when He sought to close it up,
He took two stars from Ayish (Ursa Major) and closed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of כימה and עיש from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיש follows כימה because two of its stars were used to seal the opening made in כימה for the מבול.

steps.title: Why not return the original stars?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why הקדוש ברוך הוא did not simply put כימה's own two stars back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let Him return them to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. If כימה needed two stars, why not give back its own original ones instead of taking stars from עיש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes the simplest fix is to restore the removed stars. That would have avoided taking anything from עיש and creating the 'chase'.

phrases.english: Then let Him return them to it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story told in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The detail that stars were taken from עיש rather than restoring כימה's own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Restoring the original stars seems simpler and fairer than taking stars from another constellation.

steps.title: Two answers: a pit and a prosecutor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives two answers. A pit cannot be refilled by its own dirt. And a prosecutor cannot become a defender.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pit is not filled by its own earth. Alternatively: a prosecutor does not become a defender.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two reasons why the original stars could not be put back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: just as the dirt dug from a pit is not enough to refill it, the original stars could not seal the gap. Second answer: those stars caused the destruction of the מבול, so it is not fitting for them to end it. Something that served as a קטיגור cannot act as a סניגור.

keyTerms.meaning: Its own earth (the dirt dug out of it)

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור is used elsewhere in שס too. One example is why a כהן גדול does not wear gold vestments into the קודש הקדשים, since gold recalls the golden calf.

phrases.english: A pit is not filled by its own earth.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי — אֵין קָטֵיגוֹר נַעֲשָׂה סָנֵיגוֹר.
phrases.english: Alternatively: a prosecutor does not become a defender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two independent reasons why restoration was impossible or inappropriate
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The original stars could simply be put back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The originals were either insufficient (pit) or unfit, having caused the destruction (prosecutor).

steps.title: Why not create two new stars?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why הקדוש ברוך הוא did not create two brand-new stars instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let Him create two other stars for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. If the original stars could not be used, why take from עיש rather than create new ones?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 explained why the old stars were unusable. It did not explain why another constellation had to lose stars. New stars would solve the problem without harming עיש.

phrases.english: Then let Him create two other stars for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up challenge after the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Creating new stars would avoid depriving עיש.

steps.title: Nothing new under the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from קהלת: there is nothing new under the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is nothing new under the sun.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that new creations were not added to the world, so new stars could not be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once creation was complete, the natural order was fixed. So the gap had to be filled with stars that already existed, which meant taking them from עיש.

keyTerms.meaning: There is nothing new under the sun (קהלת א:ט)

phrases.english: "There is nothing new under the sun."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: New stars could have been created.
steps.terutzMaskana: Creation is closed; no new stars are made, so existing ones had to be used.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the stars will be returned in the future
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן teaches that in the future הקדוש ברוך הוא will give the stars back to עיש. He proves it from a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will return them to it, as it says: 'And עיש will be comforted over her children.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a happy ending: עיש will one day get its 'children' back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word תנחם in the פסוק as coming from נחמה, comfort. עיש will be consoled when its stars are restored. This closes the story's tension.
steps.whatToRemember: The stars of the מבול: two were taken from כימה, and two from עיש sealed the gap. They could not be returned (pit / prosecutor), and new ones could not be created (nothing new under the sun). In the future they will be restored to עיש.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:

phrases.aramaic: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירָן לָהּ,
phrases.english: In the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will return them to it,
as it is stated: "And Ayish, over her children, You will comfort."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the כימה and עיש discussion with a future resolution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיש's stars will be restored in the future, based on ועיש על בניה תנחם.

steps.title: What are זוועות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's word זוועות and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'And over זוועות.' What are זוועות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה's list of things we make a ברכה on, and asks for a definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that over זוועות one says 'שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם'. Before applying the rule, the גמרא needs to know what event the word refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: A term from the משנה: tremors / quakes

phrases.english: "And over zeva'ot."
What are zeva'ot?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the star discussion and goes back to the next word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the משנה's term זוועות.

steps.title: רב קטינא: an earthquake
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא defines זוועות as גוהא, an earthquake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: An earthquake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא answers the question: זוועות means earthquakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this definition, the משנה's ברכה over זוועות is said when one feels an earthquake.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said: An earthquake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 7.

steps.title: רב קטינא wonders if the אוב knows what an earthquake is
steps.stepSummary: In a story, an earthquake strikes while רב קטינא passes a necromancer's house. He asks aloud whether the necromancer knows its cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא was walking on the road. When he reached the doorway of a necromancer's house, an earthquake rumbled. He said: Does this necromancer know what this earthquake is?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story, and this step sets up the next move. רב קטינא raises a question that the necromancer will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story moves from the definition (what an earthquake is) to its cause (why it happens). רב קטינא's remark is half challenge and half curiosity: does a practitioner of dark arts really have such knowledge?

keyTerms.meaning: A necromancer (one who practices אוב, consulting the dead)

phrases.english: Rav Ketina was walking along the road.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מְטָא אַפִּתְחָא דְּבֵי אוֹבָא טַמְיָא
phrases.english: When he reached the doorway of the house of a necromancer,
an earthquake rumbled.
He said: Does the necromancer know
what this earthquake is?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story about the cause of the earthquakes just defined.

steps.title: The necromancer: earthquakes are הקדוש ברוך הוא's tears
steps.stepSummary: The necromancer calls out an answer. When הקדוש ברוך הוא remembers His children suffering in exile, He drops two tears into the great sea. The sound is heard across the world, and that is an earthquake.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised his voice: Ketina, Ketina, why wouldn't I know? When הקדוש ברוך הוא remembers His children who are suffering among the nations, He sheds two tears into the great sea. Its sound is heard from one end of the world to the other, and that is an earthquake.
steps.whatsHappening: The necromancer answers רב קטינא's question and gives a spiritual cause for earthquakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earthquake is not just a natural event. It reflects הקדוש ברוך הוא's pain over the suffering of כלל ישראל in גלות. This adds meaning to the משנה's ברכה over זוועות.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer comes from a necromancer, not a חכם. Do not assume his view is the final word. Steps 11–13 evaluate it: רב קטינא calls him a liar, but the גמרא then says the two-quake detail was actually correct, and רב קטינא denied it only so people would not follow the necromancer.

phrases.english: He raised his voice to him:
Ketina, Ketina, why would I not know?

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא זוֹכֵר אֶת בָּנָיו
phrases.english: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembers His children
who dwell in suffering among the nations of the world,
He sheds two tears into the great sea,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹלוֹ נִשְׁמָע מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ,
phrases.english: and its sound is heard from one end of the world to the other,
and that is an earthquake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב קטינא's question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An earthquake is the sound of two tears הקדוש ברוך הוא drops into the great sea when He remembers His suffering children.

steps.title: רב קטינא rejects the necromancer
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says the necromancer and his statements are false.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: The necromancer is a liar, and his words are lies.
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing the necromancer’s explanation of the earthquake, רב קטינא rejects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next step explains why he thought so: the necromancer spoke of two tears, so there should have been two quakes.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said: The necromancer
is a liar, and his words are lies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the necromancer’s answer from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב קטינא declares the necromancer’s account unreliable.

steps.title: רב קטינא's reason: there should have been two earthquakes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב קטינא called the necromancer a liar. If the quake really came from two tears, there should have been two quakes, one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, shouldn’t there be an earthquake and then another earthquake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the basis for רב קטינא's rejection: the necromancer spoke of two tears, so there should have been two quakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each tear makes a sound, there should be two quakes. רב קטינא felt only one, so he concluded the necromancer's story was false.

phrases.english: If so—
shouldn’t there be one earthquake and then another?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי — גּוּהָא גּוּהָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב קטינא's rejection in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב קטינא’s declaration that the necromancer’s words are false.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The account’s two tears seem to predict two successive earthquakes.

steps.title: There were two quakes; רב קטינא hid it on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of step 12. There really were two quakes, so the necromancer's detail fit. רב קטינא refused to admit it so that people would not follow the necromancer.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not so: one earthquake does follow another. He did not acknowledge him so that everyone would not be led astray after him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of step 12. It explains that רב קטינא's public denial was deliberate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quake did come twice, just as two tears would cause, so the proof in step 12 fails. רב קטינא still called him a liar, because admitting he was right could lead people to follow a necromancer.

phrases.english: That is not so; one earthquake does follow another,
and the reason he did not acknowledge him
was so that they would not be led astray
everyone after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two-earthquake challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the observed event from the reason for רב קטינא’s public response.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one quake occurred, proving the necromancer wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail can occur; he withheld agreement to avoid leading people after the necromancer.
steps.whatToRemember: רב קטינא’s rejection does not mean the גמרא denies the detail of two successive earthquakes.

steps.title: רב קטינא’s own explanation of earthquakes
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא describes an earthquake as הקדוש ברוך הוא clapping His hands and cites a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא himself said: He claps His hands, as it says, ‘I too will strike My hand against My hand and satisfy My anger.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רב קטינא’s own explanation of the earthquake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new explanation, not another defense of the necromancer. The verse supplies the image of hands striking together.

phrases.english: And Rav Ketina himself said:
He claps His hands, as it is stated:
‘I too will strike My hand against My hand
and satisfy My anger.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining his rejection to presenting his own account.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב קטינא connects the earthquake to the scriptural image of clapping hands.

steps.title: רבי נתן explains earthquakes as a sigh
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן gives a different image and supports it with a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: He sighs, as it says, ‘I will satisfy My anger against them and be eased.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents another explanation of the earthquake, this time from רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of clapping, רבי נתן describes a sigh. His verse speaks of anger being eased.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: He sighs a sigh,
as it is stated: ‘I will satisfy My anger against them
and be eased.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different image for the same earthquake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נתן connects the earthquake to a divine sigh.

steps.title: רבנן describe a kick against the sky
steps.stepSummary: רבנן give another earthquake image and cite a verse about a powerful cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן say: He kicks the firmament, as it says, ‘He cries out like those who tread grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the explanation of רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their image is a forceful kick against the sky. The cited verse describes a powerful sound reaching the earth.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: He kicks the firmament,
as it is stated: ‘He cries out like those who tread grapes,
against all the inhabitants of the earth.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another explanation alongside the preceding ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן connect the earthquake to a forceful action against the sky.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב describes pressure beneath the throne
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב offers a fourth earthquake image, supported by a verse about the earth as a footstool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: He presses His feet beneath the כסא הכבוד, as it says, ‘The heavens are My throne, and the earth is My footstool.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents one more explanation of the earthquake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links the heavens to a throne and the earth to a footstool. רב אחא בר יעקב uses that image to explain a shaking earth.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹחֵק אֶת רַגְלָיו תַּחַת כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
phrases.english: He presses His feet beneath the throne of glory,
as it is stated: ‘Thus says the Lord:
The heavens are My throne, and the earth is My footstool.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the series of explanations for earthquakes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא בר יעקב connects the earthquake to pressure beneath the throne of glory.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has collected several different images for the earthquake; it does not choose one here.

steps.title: What does the משנה mean by thunder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה’s mention of thunder and asks what produces it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And concerning thunder: What is thunder?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves earthquakes and sets up its next topic: the thunder mentioned in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brief quotation identifies the word under discussion. The question asks for an explanation of the phenomenon.

phrases.english: And concerning thunder.
What is thunder?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next item from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What produces the sound called thunder?

steps.title: שמואל links thunder to clouds in the heavens
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers with an explanation involving clouds and supports it with a verse mentioning thunder.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Clouds in the turning heavens, as it says, ‘The sound of Your thunder was in the whirlwind; lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.’
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first answer to what thunder is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He connects the sound to clouds in the heavens. The verse places thunder together with lightning and the shaking earth.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Clouds in the turning heavens.
As it is stated: ‘The sound of Your thunder was in the whirlwind;
lightning lit up the world;
the earth trembled and shook.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first proposed answer to the thunder question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל associates thunder with clouds in the turning heavens.

steps.title: רבנן link thunder to water between clouds
steps.stepSummary: רבנן say the sound comes from clouds pouring water into one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבנן say: Clouds pour water into one another, as it says, ‘At the sound of His giving a multitude of waters in the heavens.’
steps.whatsHappening: רבנן offer a different answer to the same thunder question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their explanation centers on water moving between clouds. The verse supports it by mentioning the sound of abundant water in the heavens.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: Clouds
that pour water into one another,
as it is stated: ‘At the sound of His giving
a multitude of waters in the heavens.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another proposed source of thunder.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Thunder is the sound of clouds pouring water into one another.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב links thunder to lightning
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says a powerful flash of lightning in a cloud breaks hailstones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: A powerful lightning bolt flashes in a cloud and breaks pieces of hail.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a third explanation for thunder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His account connects the sound to a powerful lightning flash inside a cloud. The גמרא will later compare this explanation with an observed sequence.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Powerful lightning flashes in a cloud
and breaks pieces of hail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a lightning-based explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Thunder comes from powerful lightning flashing in a cloud and breaking hail.

steps.title: רב אשי compares thunder to wind across a jug
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the sound through wind blowing across openings in clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Clouds have openings. Wind comes and blows across their mouths, like wind across the mouth of a jug.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי supplies another possible way clouds make the sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug comparison helps the learner picture the proposed sound: air moves across an opening and makes a noise.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Clouds
have hollow openings,
and wind comes and blows across their mouths,
like wind across the mouth of a jug.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a wind-based explanation to the thunder discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wind blowing across openings in clouds makes a jug-like sound.

steps.title: The lightning explanation fits the observed sequence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא favors רב אחא בר יעקב’s thunder explanation because lightning is followed by rumbling clouds and rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is reasonable like רב אחא בר יעקב: lightning flashes, clouds rumble, and rain comes.
steps.whatsHappening: After listing the explanations, the גמרא says which one seems most convincing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is the sequence people observe: a flash, a rumble, and then rain. That sequence supports רב אחא בר יעקב’s link between lightning and thunder.

phrases.english: And it stands to reason like Rav Acha bar Yaakov,
for lightning flashes,
the clouds rumble, and rain comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Selects the most persuasive of the proposed explanations.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The observed sequence favors רב אחא בר יעקב’s explanation of thunder.
steps.whatToRemember: For thunder, the גמרא favors the explanation connected to lightning.

steps.title: The winds in question are strong winds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה’s winds; אביי identifies them as gale-force winds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And concerning winds: What winds? אביי said: Gale-force wind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next item from the משנה and immediately gives אביי’s answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion is not about every ordinary breeze. אביי specifies the strong wind that the passage will discuss.

phrases.english: And concerning winds: What winds?
Abaye said: Gale-force wind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from thunder to the next item in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי identifies the relevant winds as gale-force winds.

steps.title: A strong wind does not begin at night
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a received teaching that a gale-force wind does not occur at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: We have learned by tradition that a gale-force wind does not occur at night.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a received teaching about the strong wind he just identified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As worded, the teaching seems to rule out a gale-force wind at night. The גמרא will test that against what people see.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: We have learned by tradition
that a gale-force wind does not occur at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a claim about the wind that אביי identified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The received teaching says a gale-force wind does not occur at night.

steps.title: But strong winds are seen at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי’s teaching from observation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don’t we see that it does occur?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אביי’s statement does not match nighttime experience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do see gale-force winds at night. That appears to contradict the teaching as first stated.

phrases.english: But don’t we see that it does occur!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the nighttime claim with an observed counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי’s statement that a gale-force wind does not occur at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gale-force winds are visibly present at night.

steps.title: The nighttime wind began during the day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the received teaching to when the wind starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one began during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how a gale-force wind can be present at night without contradicting אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching means that such a wind does not begin at night. A wind that began by day can continue into the night.

phrases.english: That one began during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the observed nighttime wind.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the claim to the wind’s starting time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No gale-force wind can be present at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can be present at night if it began during the day.

steps.title: A strong wind does not last two full hours
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports another received teaching and attaches a verse about trouble not rising twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: We have learned by tradition that a gale-force wind does not last two hours, fulfilling the פסוק, ‘Trouble shall not rise twice.’
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second teaching about how long a gale-force wind lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching concerns duration rather than time of day. The verse supplies a phrase about trouble not rising twice.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: We have learned by tradition
that a gale-force wind does not last two hours,
fulfilling what is stated:
‘Trouble shall not rise twice.’

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a separate claim about the same kind of wind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gale-force wind does not last for two full hours.

steps.title: But strong winds seem to last longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the two-hour limit from observation.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don’t we see that it does last?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about winds that appear to continue for two hours or more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wind really remains that long, אביי’s duration limit seems wrong. The next answer will examine whether it blows without a break.

phrases.english: But don’t we see that it does last!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the stated duration limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי’s statement that a gale-force wind does not last two hours.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some gale-force winds appear to last that long.

steps.title: Brief breaks explain the longer stretch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the wind stops at intervals, so it is not one uninterrupted two-hour gale.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stops from time to time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the duration challenge by pointing to pauses in the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The overall stretch may be long, but the gale does not blow continuously throughout it. Brief interruptions keep the observation from contradicting אביי’s teaching.

phrases.english: Because it stops at intervals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the apparently long-lasting wind.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes an extended period with pauses from continuous wind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wind present over a two-hour period must have lasted continuously.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can stop briefly during that period.
steps.whatToRemember: The two answers about wind make precise distinctions: when it begins, and whether it blows continuously.

steps.title: The משנה's ברכה over lightning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that over lightning one says 'Whose strength and power fill the world.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And over lightning one says: 'Blessed… Whose strength and power fill the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה, about lightning. It is setting up a question about what this word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the side discussion about winds, the גמרא returns to the text of the משנה. The ברכה here is the same one said over other powerful natural events, such as thunder.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose strength and power fill the world

phrases.english: And over lightning one says:
'Blessed… Whose strength and power fill the world.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of winds and returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over lightning one says 'Whose strength and power fill the world.'

steps.title: What counts as lightning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by ברקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'lightning'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a clarifying question, not an attack. The גמרא wants to know exactly which sight requires the ברכה.

phrases.english: What is 'lightning'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a word in the quoted משנה.

steps.title: רבא: a flash of light
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ברקים means a flash of lightning (ברקא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a flash of light.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the משנה means ordinary flashes of lightning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He translates the Hebrew word into the common Aramaic one, so the learner knows it means normal lightning and nothing unusual.

keyTerms.meaning: A flash of lightning, a bright light

phrases.english: Rava said: a flash of light.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.

steps.title: רבא's list of warning signs in the sky
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists kinds of lightning and cloud patterns that are signs of trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: a single bolt of lightning, white lightning, green lightning, clouds that rise in the western corner and come from the southern corner, and two clouds rising facing each other: all of these are bad signs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new teaching: certain kinds of lightning and clouds warn that something bad may happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information beyond the definition. It names specific unusual sky patterns as bad omens, such as a lone bolt, odd-colored lightning, and clouds coming from unusual directions or facing each other.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
a single bolt of lightning,
and white lightning,
and green lightning,
and clouds that rise in the western corner
and come from the southern corner,
and two clouds that rise
one facing the other:
all of them are signs of trouble.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from רבא on the same topic of lightning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain lightning and cloud patterns are signs of trouble.

steps.title: Why do we need to know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes to know these signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this information matters in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often asks what we are supposed to do with a fact. Here it wants the practical use of knowing these bad signs.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical use of רבא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical purpose of knowing these signs.

steps.title: To pray for mercy
steps.stepSummary: Knowing the signs lets a person pray that no harm comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: To ask for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that when you see these signs, you should pray to ה׳ for mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs are not just predictions. They are a cue for תפילה so that the danger is prevented.

phrases.english: To pray for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical-difference question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One should pray for mercy when seeing these signs.

steps.title: Only at night, not in the morning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the warning signs to nighttime and says morning signs are meaningless.
steps.simpleTranslation: This only applies at night. In the morning they have no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit: these signs only mean something when seen at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Morning clouds and flashes have no real weight, so there is no need to worry about them. This narrows the scope of רבא's list.

phrases.english: And this applies only at night,
but in the morning they have no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבא's list to nighttime.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The trouble signs matter only at night.

steps.title: A verse: morning clouds pass away
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר יצחק supports the claim that morning clouds have no substance, citing a verse in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר יצחק said: morning clouds have no substance, as it is written: 'Your kindness is like a morning cloud.'
steps.whatsHappening: A verse is brought to back up the idea that morning clouds mean nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא compares fleeting kindness to a morning cloud that quickly disappears. This shows that morning clouds do not last, which supports the previous step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי עֲנָנֵי דְצַפְרָא לֵית בְּהוּ מְשָׁשָׁא,
phrases.english: these morning clouds have no substance,
as it is written: 'And your kindness is like a morning cloud, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim that morning signs have no substance.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse in הושע: 'וְחַסְדְּכֶם כַּעֲנַן בֹּקֶר'.

steps.title: רב פפא's challenge from a folk saying
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי about a popular saying that morning rain means it will rain all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But people say, 'When the doors open and it is raining, donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the idea that morning clouds mean nothing, using a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying tells the donkey-driver not to bother working, because rain in the morning means rain all day. So morning clouds seem to have real substance, which contradicts רבי שמואל בר יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Fold your sack and go to sleep

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But people say:
'When the doors open and there is rain,
donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, הָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim of step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that morning clouds have no substance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A common saying assumes morning rain lasts all day, so morning clouds do have substance.

steps.title: Thick clouds versus thin clouds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא distinguishes thick morning clouds, which bring rain, from light ones, which pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is when the sky is covered with thick clouds, and that is when it is covered with light clouds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The folk saying is about a sky covered with heavy, thick clouds, which bring all-day rain. רבי שמואל בר יצחק means thin clouds, which disappear quickly. Both statements are true, each in its own case.
steps.confusionAlert: In this answer, עננא means light, flimsy clouds, while עיבא means thick clouds. Do not read 'clouds' as one general category here.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is when the sky is covered with thick clouds,
that is when it is covered with light clouds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בהא, הא בהא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All morning clouds are the same, so the saying and the verse conflict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thick morning clouds bring rain, but light morning clouds pass and have no substance.

steps.title: Thunder straightens a crooked heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that thunder was created to make people fear ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: Thunder was created only to straighten the crookedness of the heart, as it says: 'And God made it so that they should fear Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching explains the purpose of thunder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thunder makes people afraid, and that fear brings them back to יראת שמים. The פסוק from קהלת shows that ה׳ made frightening things so that people would fear Him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Thunder was not created
except to straighten the crookedness of the heart,
as it is said: 'And God has made it
so that they should fear before Him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching connected to thunder, which the משנה also mentions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thunder exists to instill fear of ה׳.

steps.title: Falling on one's face at a rainbow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that one who sees a rainbow should fall on his face, based on יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלכסנדרי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: One who sees a rainbow in a cloud must fall on his face, as it says: 'Like the appearance of the bow in the cloud… and I saw, and I fell on my face.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same chain of rabbis tells us how to react to a rainbow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, the rainbow is compared to the appearance of the כבוד ה׳, and the נביא fell on his face. So a person seeing a rainbow should show the same awe.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Alexandri said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who sees the rainbow in the cloud
must fall on his face,
as it is said: 'Like the appearance of the bow
that is in the cloud, etc.
and I saw, and I fell on my face.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same rabbis, now about the rainbow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees a rainbow should fall on his face.

steps.title: In the West they opposed bowing
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they cursed anyone who fell on his face at a rainbow, because it looks like worshipping it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they cursed this, because it looks like one bowing to the rainbow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that the scholars of ארץ ישראל strongly rejected the practice of falling on one's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is מראית עין. Bowing toward a rainbow looks like worshipping a natural object, so the practice was rejected.

phrases.english: They curse this in the West,
because it looks
like one who is bowing to the rainbow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practice taught in step 42.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The practice of falling on one's face at a rainbow.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It looks like worshipping the rainbow.

steps.title: But a blessing is certainly said
steps.stepSummary: Even those who reject bowing agree that one makes a ברכה over a rainbow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a blessing, one certainly recites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that everyone agrees a ברכה is said over a rainbow. This sets up the question of what that ברכה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute was only about bowing. Making a ברכה has no risk of looking like idol worship, so it remains in place.

phrases.english: But as for a blessing, he certainly blesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rejection to bowing only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One recites a ברכה upon seeing a rainbow.

steps.title: Which blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ברכה is said over a rainbow.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he bless?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the wording of the rainbow ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know a ברכה is required. The question is only about its exact text.

phrases.english: What does he bless?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the text of the ברכה just required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The wording of the rainbow ברכה.

steps.title: Who remembers the covenant
steps.stepSummary: The ברכה is 'Blessed… Who remembers the covenant.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blessed… Who remembers the covenant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the wording: ה׳ 'remembers the covenant.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rainbow is the sign of ה׳'s promise to נח never again to destroy the world with a מבול. The ברכה praises ה׳ for remembering that ברית.

phrases.english: 'Blessed… Who remembers the covenant.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers which ברכה is said.

steps.title: A different wording from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא giving the wording 'faithful to His covenant and fulfills His word.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, says: 'Faithful to His covenant and fulfills His word.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the rainbow ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version stresses that ה׳ is faithful and keeps His promise. It does not focus on remembering. Now there are two competing wordings.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yishmael, son of
Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
'Faithful to His covenant and fulfills His word.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative wording to step 46.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה is 'נאמן בבריתו וקיים במאמרו'.

steps.title: רב פפא: say both together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that both wordings should be combined into one ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, let us say both: 'Blessed… Who remembers the covenant, is faithful to His covenant, and fulfills His word.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the question by combining the two versions into one ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are two traditions and they do not contradict each other, we satisfy both by saying them together. This is the final wording of the rainbow ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say both of them

steps.whatToRemember: Over a rainbow we do not bow, but we do say the combined ברכה: 'זוכר הברית ונאמן בבריתו וקיים במאמרו'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the ברכה said in practice today upon seeing a rainbow.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Therefore, let us say both of them:
'Blessed… Who remembers the covenant,
and is faithful to His covenant and fulfills His word.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ נֵימְרִינְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two wordings by combining them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rainbow ברכה combines both versions: זוכר הברית ונאמן בבריתו וקיים במאמרו.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on mountains and hills
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of mountains and hills, which get the ברכה 'עושה מעשה בראשית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: over mountains and hills one says 'Blessed… Who makes the work of creation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the משנה listed lightning and thunder, which get 'שכחו וגבורתו מלא עולם'. Only now, with mountains and hills, does it mention 'עושה מעשה בראשית'. That switch is what the גמרא will question.

phrases.english: Over the mountains and over the hills.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. The ברכה there is 'עושה מעשה בראשית'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rainbow ברכה to the next case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over mountains and hills one says 'עושה מעשה בראשית'.

steps.title: Isn't lightning also part of creation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: lightning and the other earlier items are also creation, as a פסוק says, so why not say 'עושה מעשה בראשית' over them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean everything we listed until now is not part of creation? But it is written: 'He made lightning for the rain'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for giving 'עושה מעשה בראשית' only to mountains, when lightning is also creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to suggest that only mountains and hills count as 'creation'. A פסוק in תהלים lists lightning among הקב"ה's acts of creation. So lightning should deserve the same ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say? (opens a challenge that rejects an implication)

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ כׇּל הָנֵי דַּאֲמַרַן עַד הַשְׁתָּא,
phrases.english: Is that to say that all these we mentioned until now,
phrases.notes: Lightning, thunder, winds, and so on, from earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: are not the work of creation?
But it is written: 'He made lightning for the rain'!
phrases.notes: תהלים קל"ה:ז. Lightning appears among the acts of creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כׇּל הָנֵי דַּאֲמַרַן עַד הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה line just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's giving 'עושה מעשה בראשית' only to mountains and hills.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that lightning is also an act of creation, so it should get the same ברכה.

steps.title: אביי: combine the two ברכות
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the two ברכות of the משנה should be joined together and applied to all its cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Join them and teach them together. Both ברכות apply to all of these items.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He says the משנה's two ברכות really belong together for every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה split the ברכות only for style. In truth, lightning also gets 'עושה מעשה בראשית', and mountains also get 'שכחו מלא עולם'. That removes the challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not adding a new ברכה. He is reading the משנה's two separate lists as one combined list.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Combine them and teach.
phrases.notes: Apply both ברכות to every case in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה (merging its two clauses)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each case in the משנה gets only the one ברכה listed next to it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברכות apply to all the cases.

steps.title: רבא: lightning fits both, mountains fit only one
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently. Over lightning both wordings fit, but over mountains only 'עושה מעשה בראשית' fits, because mountains do not show power filling the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There, over lightning, either of two ברכות fits: 'Blessed… Whose power fills the world' and 'Who makes the work of creation.' Here, over mountains, 'Who makes the work of creation' fits, but 'Whose power fills the world' does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer. The משנה's split tells us that mountains are limited to one ברכה, not that lightning is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lightning is both creation and a display of power across the world, so both wordings work. Mountains are creation but do not show power filling the world. So the משנה lists the 'power' ברכה only for lightning, and the 'creation' ברכה stays available for both.
steps.whatToRemember: Lightning and thunder: either ברכה works. Mountains and hills: only 'עושה מעשה בראשית'.

phrases.english: Rava said: There, one blesses two,
phrases.notes: Over lightning and thunder, two wordings fit.

phrases.english: 'Blessed… Whose power fills the world,'
and 'Who makes the work of creation.'
Here, 'Who makes the work of creation' applies,
but 'Whose power fills the world' does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same קשיא that אביי answered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה denies 'עושה מעשה בראשית' to lightning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lightning fits both ברכות. Mountains fit only 'עושה מעשה בראשית'.

steps.title: A clear sky gets 'Who makes creation'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that one who sees the sky in its full purity says 'עושה בראשית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One who sees the sky in its purity says, 'Blessed… Who makes creation.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching. רבי יהושע בן לוי adds another sight that gets the creation ברכה: a perfectly clear sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a case beyond what the משנה listed. A sky with no haze at all shows creation as it was first made, so it gets the same ברכה as mountains.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who sees the sky in its purity,
says: 'Blessed… Who makes creation.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הָרוֹאֶה רָקִיעַ בְּטׇהֳרָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new related ruling about the same ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Over a perfectly clear sky one says 'עושה בראשית'.

steps.title: When is the sky truly clear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the sky is actually seen in its purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. It is setting up אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'sky in its purity' is vague. The גמרא wants a concrete situation so we know when this ברכה applies.

phrases.english: When?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of רבי יהושע בן לוי's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The circumstance in which the sky appears in its purity.

steps.title: After a night of rain and a morning north wind
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains: when it rained all night and in the morning a north wind clears the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When rain falls all night, and in the morning a north wind comes and uncovers the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a specific weather situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain washes the air clean, and the north wind blows away the clouds. Then the sky is completely clear, and that is the case for the ברכה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When rain comes all night,
and in the morning a north wind comes
and uncovers the heavens.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי אָתֵי מִטְרָא כּוּלֵּי לֵילְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After an all-night rain followed by a morning north wind that clears the sky.

steps.title: This disagrees with רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יהושע בן לוי and אביי disagree with a teaching of רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with what רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a conflicting opinion. It is setting up the quote of רב חסדא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי and אביי assume a perfectly clear sky can still be seen today. The גמרא signals that רב חסדא holds otherwise, which would make this ברכה unusable nowadays.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who transmits רב חסדא's teaching

phrases.aramaic: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rafram bar Pappa who said in the name of Rav Chisda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Flags a dispute with the ruling just given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The previous ruling is noted as disputed by רב חסדא.

steps.title: No pure sky since the חורבן בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that since the בית המקדש was destroyed, the sky has not been seen in its purity, and he brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: Since the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the sky has not been seen in its purity. As it says: 'I clothe the heavens in darkness, and I make sackcloth their covering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב חסדא's teaching in full. He says a truly pure sky no longer exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the heavens wearing mourning clothes. רב חסדא reads this as a lasting sign of mourning since the חורבן. According to him, the case of רבי יהושע בן לוי can no longer happen.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי: a pure sky gets 'עושה בראשית'. רב חסדא: since the חורבן, no pure sky is seen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides whether the ברכה over a clear sky is practical today.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: For Rafram bar Pappa said in the name of Rav Chisda:
Since the day the Temple was destroyed,
the sky has not been seen in its purity,
as it says: 'I clothe the heavens in darkness,'
'and I make sackcloth their covering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the opinion that step 56 said disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, the sky has never been seen in its purity, based on ישעיהו נ:ג.
